answer: Price each seat with a refundable deposit worth more than any single identity could steal by cheating. An honest agent stakes once at dawn and draws it back whole. A farmer must bond every clone, and since one caught fraud forfeits more than it skimmed, each added head spirals the cost upward until profit is gone — the swarm's economics climb a ridge too steep to pay, and the deposit makes every copy cost real money to keep alive.
